description: p4-native's hooks. register.ts is the hooks module, whose functions run inside Claude Code, and it is the whole plugin: no command hook runs and no process starts at a session's start. At session.start it asks the engine what this host is, the surfaces the session draws on, the Claude Code version and the tools that answer, and writes the capability map to .claude/p4/native/host.json under the session's id, without the session waiting for it. It reads the map again at the first turn of the main conversation, after the session's id changed, and at session.attach and session.detach, when a surface joins the session or leaves it. probes.ts holds the watched conditions, one probe for each decision the platform blocked. The module reads them when the Claude Code version kept in .claude/p4/native/probes.json for this kind of host is not this session's, at the first turn and at that turn's end, and on request, and never at a start. An answer that changed is a notice the next prompt carries to the model once. It registers the slash command /native and the tool native, whose map, probes and probe each print what the module read. Two options of the plugin's userConfig, off by default, each make one call of Claude Code's own: push calls the PushNotification tool at the end of a turn of a session ezexe is at, or $.ui.notify where the session has no such tool, and again at classic.Notification where Claude Code says the session waits at a permission prompt or sits idle, and status pins a line that names the host by $.ui.status. weighed.json is the record of what the p4 plugins weighed, and inventory.ts holds a session's slash commands and tools against it: when the probes run, each with no row is named once, and weighed prints them on request. misses.ts is a table of situations in which a session does by hand what a native feature of this host does, with a row for each command and tool a p4 plugin uses that a session can also do by hand, and each used row of weighed.json names the rows that watch it or says why none does. The module checks it at classic.PostToolUse, where it passes on what the hooks beneath answered and adds one line of context, and at turn.complete, for the next prompt, each situation once in a session, unless the option hints is off. Each row checked at a call has an option of its own, off by default, and with one on the module refuses that by-hand call at tool.call, before it runs, with the row's line.
